title: Financial Transformation Business Analyst
location_raw: US - VA, Arlington; US - VA, McLean
description:
Job Family :
Operational Effectiveness Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 10%
Clearance Required :
Ability to Obtain Public Trust

What You Will Do:
Our Financial Management Transformation professionals help clients in Defense and National Security optimize all elements of their financial management structure by transforming business processes, enhancing operational efficiency, improving transparency and performance management, promoting change management, and ensuring compliance with Federal laws and regulations.

The nature of our projects is extremely fluid and requires self‑motivated individuals who thrive in dynamic environments and can develop solutions independently or within a team of highly skilled professionals. Project members gain opportunities to engage directly with senior client leadership and to grow their expertise in technical competency, business development, client service, and people development. Our team brings specialized knowledge in financial management, process analysis, risk management, and performance measurement to support project activities.

Guidehouse is seeking Business Analysts to support an Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) client in advancing its financial management modernization efforts. In this role, you will help evaluate current financial systems and processes, document how data and technology support today’s operations, and shape a forward‑looking roadmap that strengthens governance, integration, and strategic portfolio management. Working as part of a collaborative analyst team, you will partner closely with process owners, technical stakeholders, and OCFO leaders to clarify requirements, support decision-making, and develop the artifacts needed to establish a sustainable, enterprise-wide Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) function.

Key Responsibilities
Partner with business and technical stakeholders to assess the current state of OCFO capabilities, including feeder systems (procurement, travel, payroll, asset, grants, and other financial-related systems), data interfaces and integrations, and reporting tools and processes (including status of funds and financial statements).

- Document the system inventory and capabilities, including comprehensive discovery of all current financial, budget, procurement, and mixed systems.

- Develop the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) baseline for each application, including licensing, hosting, and maintenance costs.

- Document data flows and interfaces, manual processes and workarounds, and pain points, risks, and audit findings related to systems and reporting.

- Contribute to the Current State Assessment Report, including findings, gaps, and opportunities for consolidation, modernization, and automation.

- Assess current capabilities and capability gaps against strategic priorities, plans, goals, and objectives, and develop and assess requirements needed to close identified gaps.

- Establish metrics to ensure projects meet their objectives and mitigate documented capability gaps, and support information technology (IT) financial governance processes, standards, and performance metrics.

- Assist with Analyses of Alternatives (AoA) for solution requests and support design and implementation of the SPM Implementation Roadmap.

- Prepare briefings, decision papers, and meeting materials for an OCFO Governance Board; document decisions, action items, and risks; and track progress against the modernization roadmap.

- Contribute to monthly status reports covering accomplishments, upcoming activities, risks, issues, and performance metrics.

- Develop user guides, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and technical documentation; support delivery of training to Government users and support staff on governance and SPM processes; and support transition and knowledge transfer activities.

What You Will Need:

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance/Accounting, Information Technology, Program Management, or a related field.

- FIVE (5) years of relevant experience in business analysis, financial management, financial, financial governance, systems, or IT portfolio management, preferably in a federal environment.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

- Experience supporting a federal OCFO, preferably within DHS.

- Familiarity with OMB Circulars A-123 and A-130, FFMIA, FISMA, FITARA, DHS MD 102-01, and federal financial management system requirements.

- Experience with IT portfolio governance, capital planning and investment control (CPIC), or strategic portfolio management practices.

- Certifications such as PMP or Lean Six Sigma.

- Ability to read, interpret, and develop financial management procedural documents.

- Ability to read, interpret, and apply legislative and governing authorities to develop financial management policy, regulations, and directives.

- Ability to develop briefing papers, materials, and graphical presentations, and deliver formal oral presentations to all levels of Government personnel.

- Ability to research, benchmark, educate, and inform management on alternatives for delivery of financial services.

- Ability to facilitate decisions vertically and horizontally within complex Government organizations.

- Experience with system inventories, TCO analysis, AoA, requirements development, or financial systems modernization efforts.

- Eligibility for a favorable DHS Public trust EOD and fitness determination.

What You Will Do:
As a Senior Data Analyst, you will be part of a dynamic team supporting customers within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). In this role, you will help drive data‑informed decision‑making by collecting, transforming, integrating, and analyzing data to identify trends, assess performance, and create meaningful visualizations. Senior Data Analyst is responsible for identifying, assessing, protecting, and monitoring the organization’s High Value Assets (HVAs)—the systems, data, and services whose compromise would significantly impact mission, operations, or security. This role blends cybersecurity expertise, data analytics, and risk management to ensure HVAs are properly cataloged, continuously monitored, and safeguarded against evolving threats.

- Collect, integrate, and analyze complex datasets to uncover insights that support mission objectives.

- Perform quantitative and qualitative risk assessments focused on threats, vulnerabilities, and potential impacts to HVAs.

- Use analytics tools to build dashboards, key risk indicators (KRIs), and trend analyses that support leadership decisions.

- Develop intuitive, interactive, and visually compelling dashboards (e.g., in Power BI) for users with a wide range of technical backgrounds.

- Define data requirements and ensure data is properly stored, accessible, and aligned with client needs.

- Create and maintain data governance documentation, tools, and templates.

- Collaborate with non‑technical stakeholders to gather, understand, and refine requirements.

- Identify and document data quality and fidelity issues; provide recommendations for remediation.

- Build tools, resources, and reports to support data requests and ongoing analysis needs.

- Operate effectively in a hybrid work environment, including on‑site client work, Guidehouse offices, and remote settings.

What You Will Need:

- Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust (or higher) security clearance.

- Bachelor's degree.

- TWELEVE (12) or more years of experience in data analysis, engineering, data visualization, data integration, or database management OR TEN (10) years of experience with a Masters degree.

- Experience ensuring data accuracy and usability through data quality management and integration using tools such as SQL, Python, or R.

- Experience creating data visualizations and dashboards with Power BI.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

- Knowledge of federal or enterprise HVA requirements and cybersecurity frameworks.

- Ability to interpret complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Understanding of relational database design and structures.

- Hands‑on experience with data wrangling and analysis in R or Python.

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively on cross‑functional teams.

The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team’s work supports developers, operators and sponsors to bring in new grid-scale and community renewables, storage and green fuels resources. Our Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team develops and maintains a suite of quantitative market models that Guidehouse’s clients, renewable and storage players, and utilities depend on for capital investment decisions, business improvement and grid reliability. Through our wholesale and retail market expertise and modeling capabilities, we forecast energy market conditions across North America, along with generating resource additions and retirements, intra-day commercial optimization of assets using different market instruments, in an effort to identify business opportunities and quantify business risks. The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team maintains its independent view of North American wholesale power markets in its bi-annual Reference Case.

Responsibilities of a Senior Consultant include, but are not limited to, the following:

- Supporting large and complex client engagements.

- Tracking and analyzing energy market trends.

- Translating clients' inquiries and challenges into actionable scopes of work.

- Compiling reports, presentations, and other documents to communicate solutions, strategies, and analysis to clients.

- Developing and using analytical models, programming, and simulations to forecast market prices, conduct research and development, and create tools to improve productivity and accuracy.

- Reviewing and approving model outputs via data collection, manipulation, and analyses, which may involve spreadsheet and database creation and management.

On our team you’ll:

- Develop expertise in ISO/RTO markets across North America, at the crossroads of local energy pricing, capacity auctions, ancillary services and shifts in load composition and demand response initiatives

- Be intimately familiar with the economics, policies and players driving renewables, battery storage development, green fuels and new power generation technologies.

- Supervise simulations of the future dispatch of the power transmission grid using an economic dispatch model.

- Review the addition/retirement of diverse generating resources using a capacity expansion model across ISO/RTO markets.

- Understand how energy players procure power, integrate renewables, and maintain grid reliability.

- Help develop our Reference Case while expanding our client base.

description:

Job Description Summary
The Data Analyst – Solution Architecture Support will provide analytical, documentation, data modeling, and data-driven decision support for a large-scale agile software development and platform modernization program supporting the GrantSolutions contract. This role will work closely with the Solution Architect, Product Owners, engineering teams, enterprise architects, data architects, vendors, and Federal stakeholders to analyze current-state processes, data flows, interface dependencies, data models, reporting needs, and modernization impacts. The Data Analyst will help translate business and technical information into clear artifacts that support architecture decisions, integration planning, data governance, release readiness, data model alignment, and long-term platform modernization objectives.

What You Will Do :
We are seeking a detail-oriented Data Analyst to support the Solution Architect on a large-scale GrantSolutions platform modernization effort. This role will help analyze business processes, data structures, conceptual and logical data models, system interfaces, reporting needs, and modernization dependencies to inform solution design and technical execution across multiple workstreams, vendors, and Scrum teams.

The Data Analyst will support the Solution Architect by gathering, analyzing, validating, modeling, and documenting data and process information needed to guide modernization decisions. This individual will develop clear analysis artifacts, data mappings, data model views, entity relationship summaries, interface inventories, workflow summaries, decision support materials, and stakeholder-ready documentation. The role requires strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, communication skills, and the ability to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders to support architecture alignment, data quality, data modeling, integration planning, governance, and incremental transition from legacy capabilities to modernized services.

- Support the Solution Architect by analyzing current-state processes, data flows, system interfaces, reporting needs, and modernization dependencies across legacy and modernized capabilities.

- Develop and maintain data mapping artifacts, conceptual and logical data model views, entity relationship summaries, interface inventories, source-to-target documentation, process flows, dependency logs, and analysis summaries that inform architecture and implementation decisions.

- Gather and validate business, data, and reporting requirements from Product Owners, Federal stakeholders, vendors, subject matter experts, and delivery teams.

- Analyze data quality, data lineage, system-of-record considerations, duplicate data paths, synchronization needs, data model alignment, and integration impacts to support modernization planning.

- Support development and validation of conceptual, logical, and implementation-oriented data models by identifying key entities, relationships, attributes, business rules, data domains, and model impacts across legacy and modernized capabilities.

- Translate complex business and technical information into clear documentation, visuals, decision summaries, briefing materials, and stakeholder-ready analysis products.

- Support architecture review, design discussions, trade-off analysis, release readiness reviews, and dependency management by preparing evidence-based analysis and concise summaries.

- Coordinate with engineering, testing, DevSecOps, data, security, and vendor teams to confirm assumptions, clarify data needs, document open questions, and track follow-up actions.

- Assist with analysis of API-enabled services, shared platform capabilities, data exchange patterns, workflow automation, interoperability needs, and legacy coexistence considerations.

- Identify and communicate risks, gaps, inconsistencies, and dependencies related to data, interfaces, workflows, requirements, reporting, testing, and operational transition planning.

- Maintain organized analysis repositories, working documents, traceability materials, and status inputs to support coordinated modernization execution and leadership visibility.

What You Will Need :

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.

- Bachelor’s degree required.

- Minimum of THREE (3) years of experience in data analysis, business analysis, systems analysis, requirements analysis, reporting, data governance, systems integration support, or related roles.

- Experience analyzing data structures, conceptual and logical data models, business processes, system interfaces, reporting requirements, source-to-target mappings, data quality issues, or workflow dependencies.

- Strong understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), agile delivery concepts, requirements traceability, data analysis practices, and collaboration across technical and business teams.

- Ability to collect, interpret, validate, and document data and process information from multiple sources, stakeholders, systems, and delivery teams.

- Ability to develop clear analysis artifacts such as data mappings, data model views, entity relationship summaries, process flows, interface inventories, requirements summaries, dependency trackers, gap analyses, and decision support materials.

- Familiarity with APIs, data exchange concepts, relational databases, conceptual and logical data modeling, reporting tools, query logic, data lineage, system-of-record concepts, and interoperability across legacy and modernized systems.

- Experience working with cross-functional teams, including product, engineering, testing, architecture, security, data, vendor, and stakeholder groups.

- Ability to identify and communicate risks, gaps, assumptions, inconsistencies, and dependencies in a clear and actionable manner.

- Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Visio or similar diagramming tools, and collaboration platforms used to document and manage analysis work.

- Strong problem-solving, critical-thinking, organization, and attention-to-detail skills.

- Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills with a team-first mindset and solution-oriented approach.

- Ability to translate detailed analysis into clear narratives, visuals, summaries, and recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.

- Self-motivated, adaptable, and able to operate effectively in fast-paced, dynamic environments with guidance from the Solution Architect and program leadership.

What Would Be Nice To Have :

- Experience supporting federal or government IT programs involving grants management, legacy system modernization, shared services, interoperability, cloud adoption, data governance, or phased capability delivery.

- Experience supporting solution architecture, enterprise architecture, data architecture, application modernization, or systems integration teams.

- Understanding of AWS data architectures and cloud security principles, including secure data storage, data lifecycle management, encryption, identity and access management (IAM), key management (AWS KMS), and governance best practices to support secure, scalable, and compliant cloud solutions.

- Familiarity with SQL, data profiling, reporting dashboards, data visualization, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analysis and reporting tools.

- Familiarity with API documentation, interface control documents, canonical data models, conceptual and logical data models, entity relationship diagrams, data dictionaries, data catalogs, or metadata management practices.

- Experience working in agile delivery environments using tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence, SharePoint, or similar collaboration and work management platforms.

- Data, agile, business analysis, cloud, or analytics certification preferred, such as CBAP, PMI-PBA, Certified ScrumMaster, SAFe, AWS Cloud Practitioner, Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst, or similar credentials.

- Experience using generative AI and AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Amazon Q, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Amazon Bedrock, or similar) to accelerate data analysis, SQL generation, documentation, workflow automation, requirements analysis, and technical problem solving.

title: Cloud and Health AI FinOps and Technology Value Optimization
description:
Job Family :
Technology Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 50%
Clearance Required :
None

We are seeking a senior leader to build and lead our Cloud and AI FinOps and Technology Value Optimization capability for healthcare provider clients. This is a portfolio role, not a single-engagement role. The successful candidate will carry concurrent delivery accountability across multiple health system clients, own the commercial performance of that portfolio, shape the methodologies and assets that make the capability repeatable, and serve as the practice's most credible voice with CFOs, CIOs, and Chief Data and AI Officers on what cloud and AI actually cost and what value they actually return.
The immediate anchor assignment is a large academic medical center's Azure migration, where this leader will own a two-workstream program spanning cloud FinOps enablement and organizational change management. That engagement is the entry point to a broader agenda: as health systems move workloads and stand up AI platforms, they are discovering that consumption-based economics, fragmented application portfolios, and immature governance compound each other. This leader will connect those problems — FinOps discipline, application and AI workload rationalization, cloud operating model design, and the change management required to make any of it stick — into a coherent point of view and a growing book of work.
This role suits someone who is equally comfortable in front of a finance committee defending a commitment strategy, in a working session with cloud engineers debating tagging enforcement, and in a practice leadership meeting arguing for where to invest next. It carries real autonomy, real revenue accountability, and a clear path to Partner-track responsibility.

What You Will Do:
Client and Portfolio Leadership

- Hold delivery and commercial accountability for a portfolio of concurrent cloud and AI FinOps, rationalization, and technology value optimization engagements, including scope, quality, margin, staffing, risk posture, and client satisfaction across all of them.

- Serve as the senior client-facing voice with CFOs, CIOs, Chief Data and AI Officers, and their governance committees — framing tradeoffs, defending recommendations under scrutiny, and converting analysis into decisions leadership is willing to fund and act on.

- Set the standard for executive deliverables across the portfolio, personally shaping the narrative, structure, and defensibility of board- and committee-level materials rather than reviewing them at the margin.

- Manage the balance between advisory posture and hands-on execution, deploying the team into direct build work where client capacity is constrained without allowing the engagement to drift into unpriced staff augmentation.

Cloud and AI FinOps

- Lead establishment of durable FinOps capabilities for cloud and AI workloads, spanning consumption baselining, cost allocation and unit economics, showback and chargeback design, forecasting, anomaly management, and value realization tracking.

- Advise clients on enterprise agreement and commitment strategy, including commitment sizing and right-sizing, reservation and savings plan portfolios, consumption trajectory risk, and the financial exposure created by aggressive multi-year commitments.

- Bring a defensible point of view on AI and analytics workload economics — GPU and inference cost behavior, consumption-based data platform pricing, model and token-level attribution, and the shared-service allocation problems that make AI spend uniquely difficult to govern.

- Direct design of cloud operating model components that sustain FinOps beyond the engagement: Cloud Center of Excellence structures, intake and provisioning workflows, tagging taxonomies and enforcement automation, decision rights, policy guardrails, and recurring cost review routines.

- Oversee automation and reporting build-out across native cloud cost management tooling, data platform usage telemetry, and enterprise BI, ensuring clients inherit working instrumentation rather than a static assessment.

Cloud and AI Rationalization and Value Optimization

- Lead application and workload rationalization engagements, including portfolio inventory and segmentation, disposition analysis, cloud candidacy and workload placement criteria, migration wave sequencing, and the business cases that justify retire, consolidate, replatform, or modernize decisions.

- Extend rationalization discipline to the emerging AI estate — redundant models, pilots, copilots, and point solutions — and help clients distinguish AI investments that are compounding value from those that are accumulating cost and risk.

- Connect rationalization findings to run-rate reduction, contract and licensing optimization, technical debt retirement, and reinvestment capacity, quantified in terms finance leadership will stand behind.

- Partner with enterprise architecture, infrastructure, security, and data leaders to ensure disposition and placement recommendations account for interoperability, regulatory, data retention, and risk constraints specific to healthcare.

Change Enablement and Adoption

- Hold accountability for the organizational change management workstreams attached to cloud and AI programs, directing change strategy, stakeholder and impact assessment, communications, change networks, role-based training, and adoption measurement through dedicated change leads.

- Ensure the operating model and cost governance work is matched by genuine organizational adoption, treating readiness and behavior change as delivery outcomes rather than supporting activities.

Practice Building and Growth

- Originate and close follow-on and net-new work across the portfolio, including scoping, pricing, proposal development, and oral presentations, with accountability for an annual sales or expansion target.

- Build the reusable methodologies, accelerators, maturity models, benchmarks, and pricing constructs that turn repeated engagement work into a scalable practice capability.

- Represent the firm externally through thought leadership, conference participation, client roundtables, and hyperscaler and platform partner relationships that generate pipeline.

- Recruit, develop, and performance-manage consultants through senior manager level across FinOps, cloud engineering, application portfolio, and change management skill sets, and serve as career advisor to a group of professionals.

What You Will Need:

- Minimum of SEVEN (7)+ years of overall work experience.

- Bachelors degree from an accredited university.

- Experience in technology consulting, cloud and technology financial management, or technology transformation.

- Experience in engagement leadership level with accountability for delivery outcomes and commercial performance.

- Demonstrated ownership of a portfolio of concurrent engagements — not sequential single-project leadership — including staffing across teams, margin management, and executive relationship ownership at multiple accounts simultaneously.

- Deep command of cloud economics on at least one major hyperscaler, with Microsoft Azure strongly preferred, including enterprise agreements and commitment constructs, native cost management tooling, reservations and savings plans, tagging and policy enforcement, and allocation across shared and dedicated services.

- Track record establishing FinOps capabilities aligned to recognized frameworks across the inform, optimize, and operate domains, with evidence of capabilities that persisted after the consulting team departed.

- Substantive experience in application portfolio rationalization, workload placement, or technology cost reduction, including disposition frameworks, business case development, and executive decision governance.

- Working fluency in AI and data platform economics, including consumption-based analytics platforms, GPU and inference cost drivers, and the attribution challenges created by shared AI and analytics services.

- Demonstrated accountability for organizational change management as an integrated workstream, including change strategy, adoption measurement, and executive-level stakeholder management.

- Proven ability to sell — origination, scoping, pricing, proposal leadership, and closing — with a credible record of revenue generated or expanded.

- Executive presence sufficient to hold a room of C-suite healthcare leaders, including the judgment to deliver unwelcome findings about cost exposure, failed governance, or unrealistic business cases without losing the relationship.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

- Experience serving academic medical centers, integrated delivery networks, and other healthcare provider organizations, including fluency with service line economics, fund and grant accounting, research computing, and public institution procurement and governance constraints.

- Familiarity with the healthcare platforms that drive the majority of cloud and AI consumption, including Epic and Oracle Health ecosystems, enterprise data platforms, imaging, and clinical and research analytics workloads.

- FinOps Certified Professional credentials, Prosci or equivalent change management certification, and Azure architecture certifications; familiarity with the Cloud Adoption Framework and Well-Architected Framework.

- Experience building a consulting capability or offering from an early stage to a repeatable, multi-client business, including methodology development, pricing strategy, and team build-out.

- Established relationships with hyperscaler and platform partner field organizations that translate into co-sell pipeline.

- Experience with adjacent scopes that extend cloud FinOps engagements, including multi-cloud and SaaS spend management, sustainability and carbon reporting, and enterprise technology business management.

- Advanced degree such as an MBA, MHA, or master's in information systems, and a record of published thought leadership or conference speaking in cloud economics, AI governance, or healthcare technology strategy.

- US Citizenship is contractually required.

About the Role:
Healthcare organizations are committing to cloud and AI at a pace that has outrun their ability to govern the spend or prove the return. Commitments are signed before consumption is understood, workloads migrate before portfolios are rationalized, and AI pilots multiply faster than anyone can measure what they cost. The leader in this role will be the person clients call when they need that situation made legible and then fixed — and will build the team, methods, and market position that let the firm answer that call at scale. Success looks like clients who can defend every dollar of cloud and AI spend, portfolios that are meaningfully smaller and better governed, and a practice capability that outlasts any single engagement.

Job Description Summary
The Business/Systems Analyst will support requirements analysis, process definition, stakeholder engagement, and solution alignment for a large-scale agile software development and platform modernization program supporting the GrantSolutions contract. This role is responsible for eliciting, documenting, analyzing, and validating business needs, system requirements, workflows, data exchanges, integration dependencies, and operational impacts across multiple workstreams and Scrum teams. The Business/Systems Analyst will work closely with Product Owners, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, enterprise architects, vendors, Federal stakeholders, and end users to translate modernization objectives into clear, actionable requirements and support high-quality outcomes across the system development lifecycle.

What You Will Do :
We are seeking a strong Business/Systems Analyst to support requirements, process, and solution analysis for a large-scale GrantSolutions platform modernization effort. This role will work across business stakeholders, Federal users, vendors, architects, and agile delivery teams to define current-state and future-state workflows, clarify business needs, document functional and non-functional requirements, and support incremental capability delivery while maintaining continuity of the legacy system throughout the transition.
The Business/Systems Analyst will help bridge business operations, user needs, system functionality, data exchanges, and technical delivery in an iterative modernization environment. This individual will analyze and document requirements for a modern integration layer that enables new vendor-delivered capabilities to interface with legacy components as the modernized platform is built out over time. title: AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer
description:
Job Family :
Software Development & Support
Travel Required :
None
Clearance Required :
Ability to Obtain Public Trust

AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer
We are seeking an AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer to design, implement, and operate the cloud-native data platform that powers AI/ML, analytics, reporting, and data visualization. You will build a modern lakehouse on Amazon S3 using AWS-native services and open table formats, providing Databricks-like capabilities while maintaining portability, strong governance, cost efficiency, and operational control. You will also develop scalable batch and streaming ingestion, Python and PySpark ETL/ELT pipelines, metadata and governance services, and automated cloud provisioning and CI/CD across environments.
This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys platform building, automation, performance optimization, and enabling advanced analytics through trusted, secure, and well-governed data.

What You Will Do

Build and Operate Data Pipelines (Batch and Streaming)

- Design and implement batch and streaming ingestion from APIs, relational databases, file drops, event streams, and external partners.

- Implement, test, and optimize ETL/ELT pipelines using Python and PySpark to produce curated, analytics-ready datasets for reporting, visualization, and machine learning.

- Implement incremental processing, change data capture (CDC), data contracts, schema validation, and reusable transformation frameworks.

- Improve pipeline reliability through automated testing, orchestration, monitoring, retry handling, and operational runbooks.

Deliver an AWS-Native Lakehouse Data Platform

- Design and implement a Delta Lakehouse-style data platform using AWS-native services to provide Databricks-like capabilities for data engineering, analysis, and data visualization.

- Build and manage a scalable lakehouse on Amazon S3 using Apache Iceberg and open columnar formats such as Apache Parquet.

- Implement SQL-like table reliability for data stored in Amazon S3, including ACID transactions, schema evolution, partition evolution, snapshot isolation, time travel, and rollback capabilities using Apache Iceberg.

- Enable fast, interactive querying of lakehouse data using AWS-native query and compute services such as Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Redshift where appropriate.

- Optimize performance and cost through partitioning, compaction, file sizing, statistics, caching, lifecycle policies, and efficient separation of compute and storage.

- Establish standardized development, test, and production environments with consistent configuration and controlled promotion across stages.

Metadata, Governance, Access Control, Lineage, and Quality

- Implement data governance and fine-grained access control using AWS-native services, including AWS Lake Formation, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS Key Management Service (KMS), and related security services.

- Implement a managed metadata repository for dataset cataloging, ownership, business definitions, tagging, classification, and discoverability.

- Enable end-to-end lineage from source through transformation and consumption to support auditability, impact analysis, and regulatory requirements.

- Apply policy-based access, least-privilege permissions, row-, column-, and cell-level controls where required, data classification, retention, encryption, and secure data handling.

- Build operational data quality checks for freshness, completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, and anomaly detection, and publish measurable SLAs/SLOs.

AWS Automation, CI/CD, and Operations

- Implement automated AWS provisioning using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to create consistent environments and secure-by-default baselines.

- Build and enhance CI/CD for data pipelines and lakehouse components, including automated tests, security checks, validation gates, packaging, deployment, promotion, and rollback strategies.

- Implement observability with centralized metrics, logs, traces, alerts, dashboards, runbooks, and incident-response procedures.

- Continuously evaluate platform performance, scalability, reliability, security, and cost, and implement measurable improvements.

Cross-Team Collaboration and Documentation

- Work closely with data, application, analytics, AI/ML, security, networking, and cloud platform teams to support mission needs and delivery timelines.

- Maintain high-quality engineering documentation, including architecture diagrams, data models, SOPs, interface specifications, operational runbooks, and secure configuration baselines.

- Present technical findings, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What You Will Need

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related field, or FOUR (4) years equivalent practical experience in leu of degree.

- SIX (6) years of relevant experience.

- Hands-on experience implementing AWS-native data lake or lakehouse architectures using Amazon S3 and services such as AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Lake Formation, and Amazon Redshift.

- Strong experience developing production ETL/ELT pipelines using Python and PySpark, including data modeling, transformation, testing, performance tuning, and error handling.

- Hands-on experience with Apache Iceberg, including ACID transactions, snapshots, schema and partition evolution, time travel, table maintenance, and query optimization.

- Advanced SQL skills and experience supporting analytical queries, semantic layers, reporting tools, and data visualization workloads.

- Experience implementing metadata management and governance capabilities, including cataloging, lineage, ownership, classification, policy enforcement, and fine-grained access controls.

- Experience with AWS security fundamentals, including IAM and least privilege, KMS encryption, secrets management, network security, logging, and secure SDLC practices.

- Experience provisioning AWS resources using IaC and operating data platforms across multiple environments.

- Experience building or operating CI/CD pipelines for data workflows, including testing, packaging, deployment automation, environment promotion, and rollback.

- Ability to troubleshoot distributed data-processing workloads and optimize performance, reliability, and cost.

What Would Be Nice to Have

- Hands-on experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, or migrating Databricks workloads to AWS-native services and Apache Iceberg.

- Experience with AWS Step Functions, Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA), Amazon Kinesis, AWS Database Migration Service (DMS), AWS Lambda, Amazon MSK, or similar ingestion and orchestration services.

- Experience with modern DevOps practices and tools such as Git, Terraform, AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK, Jenkins, AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, and Docker.

- Experience integrating lakehouse data with business intelligence and visualization tools such as Amazon QuickSight, Tableau, or Power BI.

- Experience using AI-assisted coding tools, such as GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor, or Kiro, to accelerate implementation while maintaining code quality, testing, review, privacy, and security controls.

- Knowledge graph and Graph RAG experience, including graph modeling, ontology and taxonomy alignment, entity resolution, relationship extraction, and hybrid retrieval that combines graph traversal with semantic or vector search.
